headline: In 1958 the US Air Force studied setting off a nuclear bomb on the Moon.
slides: Officially 'A Study of Lunar Research Flights'. Secret, ordered by the US Air Force.
To show the world, and the Soviets, what America could do. The flash would be visible from Earth.
Physicist Leonard Reiffel led about ten people in Chicago.
A 24-year-old Carl Sagan was on it, modelling how the dust cloud would spread in low gravity.
The plan was dropped in 1959. Reiffel worried about the cost to science of contaminating the Moon.
Nobody knew until Reiffel, then 73, told the press. The Air Force has never commented.
sources: Sources: Leonard Reiffel interview (The Observer, 2000), Keay Davidson 'Carl Sagan: A Life', USAF A119 reports 1958-59
